newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ATHLETICS-CASTRO WINS ROTTERDAM MARATHON IN YEAR'S BEST TIME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CASTRO WINS ROTTERDAM MARATHON IN YEAR'S BEST TIME.

text.p: Portugal's Domingos Castro won the Rotterdam Marathon on Sunday in two hours seven minutes 51 seconds, the year's best time.
Alejandro Gomes of Spain was second in his first ever marathon in 2:07.54 and Sammy Korir of Kenya finished third in 2:08.02.
"The time is fantastic. A good time was most important to me, winning came second," said Castro.
The Portuguese runner completed the distance four seconds faster than the winning time of 2:07.55 recorded by his compatriot Antonio Pinto in the London Marathon a week ago.
Rotterdam is the world's fastest marathon course with the world record of 2:06.50 set by Belayneh Densamo of Ethiopia still intact after nine years.
Runners say the course has become even faster now that organisers have replaced the tricky Willems Bridge over the river Maas with the new Erasmus Bridge which is less steep.
But the pace in the first 10 kms was slower than expected due to cautious running by the pacemakers.
A large pack formed at the front of the field which was slowly whittled down to 12 runners with Densamo, a four-times winner in Rotterdam, dropping behind before the 15-km mark.
The 12 front-runners stayed together until the 33-year-old Castro and Korir stepped up the pace.
Only three others, Gomes, Abebe Mekkonen of Ethiopia and Simon Lopuyet of Kenya, could keep up the pace, but at 40 kms Mekkonen and Lopuyet fell further behind.
Castro eventually broke clear, pursued only by Gomes some 20 metres behind him, to claim his first victory in a marathon.
In the women's race, which drew only a few entries, Kenya's Tegla Loroupe won in 2:22.07, not only the best time so far this year but also a personal best and a Kenyan record.
Marleen Renders of Belgium finished second in 2:25.56, also improving her personal best and the national record.
